title: Collections Ladder
user: A freelancer or 2–10 person service business that needs to chase a late invoice firmly without losing the client relationship.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ask HN describes overdue-invoice chasing as manual and awkward; it reports businesses falling back from QB/Xero reminders to WhatsApp or simply letting debts slide, and received 30 comments.
A self-hosted Invoice Ninja user reports a plausible reminder state in which no further reminders are sent after an outage/import, and asks for a safer recovery flow.

recurrence: Two independent 2026 reports, including a 30-comment Ask HN thread; non-payment is directly cash-flow threatening and reminder-state failures are easy to miss.
current_workaround: Use accounting-suite reminders, send ad-hoc email/WhatsApp nudges, or maintain a spreadsheet of who needs chasing.
incumbents_and_gap: QuickBooks, Xero, FreshBooks, and Invoice Ninja can send reminders, but leave a small operator without an explicit escalation ladder, recovery state, and relationship-sensitive next-action queue.
smallest_useful_product: Local-first PWA: import a CSV of invoices, define a 3–5 step cadence, record contact attempts/promises/disputes, and generate the next editable email/WhatsApp-ready message. Non-goals: payment processing, debt collection, legal advice, or autonomous sending.
success_measure: In a 30-day pilot, 70% of overdue invoices are assigned a next action and median days with no follow-up drops by 50%.
monetization: one-time — a small operator should own a simple local collections workflow without a percentage or per-reminder fee.
constraints: Store client/contact data locally by default; provide export/delete; message templates must be editable and avoid legal claims or harassment automation.
why_distinct: It is a human-controlled collections state machine, not another invoicing system or AI email writer.

title: Reminder Mailroom
user: A solo business that must retain one canonical invoice record in an accounting archive while still sending normal payment reminders.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A former small-business owner says repeatedly writing the same three-week overdue follow-up was painful enough to build a tool around it.
A user BCCs invoices to accounting for archive/matching, but reminder emails create duplicate accounting records and asks for mail-type-specific routing.

recurrence: Two independent 2026 invoice-reminder reports; duplicate records turn otherwise useful follow-ups into reconciliation work.
current_workaround: BCC every email and manually delete duplicates, turn off archival forwarding for reminders, or archive PDFs by hand.
incumbents_and_gap: Invoice Ninja, QuickBooks, and Xero handle sending and accounting, but their outbound-mail rules do not consistently distinguish original delivery from reminder/archive copies across providers.
smallest_useful_product: A local SMTP/IMAP companion that labels invoice emails by subject/thread rules, forwards only the first canonical invoice or a deduplicated PDF hash to an archive mailbox, and keeps an audit log. Non-goals: invoice generation, bookkeeping, or reading arbitrary mail without explicit rules.
success_measure: Pilot users reduce duplicate invoice archive entries by at least 90% while preserving one searchable original for 100% of configured invoice threads.
monetization: one-time — the value is a privacy-respecting personal mail rule, not a hosted communications platform.
constraints: Use OAuth where required; encrypt local credentials; make forwarding rules visible and reversible; never transmit full mail content to analytics.
why_distinct: It fixes the accounting-archive side effect of chasing invoices rather than competing as an invoice sender.

title: Quote Review Gate
user: A tiny agency where a junior estimator prepares a quote but an owner needs to check price, scope, and wording before it reaches a client.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A freelancer-built proposal product was motivated by juggling PDFs, e-signature tools, invoices, and unclear client response status.
A self-hosted user explicitly requests Submit for Approval, approve/send or deny/send-back-with-comment because duplicate or erroneous quotes can reach clients.

recurrence: Two independent 2026 sources identify the quote-to-send handoff as a separate workflow; sending a wrong price or duplicate quote has immediate credibility and margin cost.
current_workaround: Email PDFs to an owner, use chat approval, or share an accounting-suite login with broad permissions.
incumbents_and_gap: Invoice Ninja has a requested approval feature; CRMs and PSA suites offer deep workflows but are expensive and overbroad for a two-person studio.
smallest_useful_product: A shareable local quote-review page: upload or paste a quote, flag price/scope fields, request one approver, collect approve/changes/decline plus a timestamped comment, then export a send-ready PDF/email. Non-goals: e-signature, CRM, invoice creation, or payment collection.
success_measure: At least 80% of pilot quotes receive an explicit recorded decision before sending, with zero unapproved quote sends in 60 days.
monetization: freemium — a free single-owner review flow validates use; paid teams need several approvers and retention.
constraints: Quote values and client identities are sensitive; use expiring signed links, access revocation, and configurable retention; do not imply legally binding approval.
why_distinct: It is a narrow pre-send control for a quote artifact, not a sales CRM or generic document approval suite.

title: Client Decision Receipt
user: A freelancer who needs a clear, client-visible yes/no/change decision on a proposal rather than ambiguous views or an undocumented call.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A proposal-tracking launch says freelancers get no visibility after sending; a commenter challenges read tracking as noise because it does not determine the next action.
A self-hosted user found the Quote Sent webhook stayed silent while the invoice webhook worked, blocking an intended Paperless/n8n integration.

recurrence: Two 2026 sources show a gap between a quote being sent/viewed and a dependable operational signal; it blocks work from starting cleanly.
current_workaround: Watch email, chase manually, use a read receipt, or rely on brittle webhooks and then reconstruct the verbal decision later.
incumbents_and_gap: PandaDoc, DocuSign, and proposal suites emphasize signatures and analytics; accounting tools expose lifecycle events inconsistently. A tiny business often only needs an unambiguous decision and scope snapshot.
smallest_useful_product: A hosted decision link with Accept, Request changes, or Decline; selected line items/scope are frozen into a dated receipt and emailed to both parties. Non-goals: legally regulated e-signature, proposal authoring, surveillance pixels, or invoice sync.
success_measure: Over 60 days, 60% of proposals sent through the product return a recorded decision and fewer than 10% need a follow-up asking what the client decided.
monetization: freemium — low-volume freelancers need a free trustworthy decision link; branded domains and archives can fund it.
constraints: Clearly label it as an acknowledgement unless a compliant e-signature flow is added; retain immutable receipt hashes; support deletion and data export.
why_distinct: It replaces passive open tracking with an explicit, portable decision receipt.

title: Subclient Worklog
user: A subcontractor who bills an agency but must prove time and deliverables against the agency’s end client or project.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A freelancer time-tracking launch says existing tools feel bloated, invasive, or web-only, and frames contract work as the use case.
A subcontractor feature request says invoices answer who pays but not whose work it is for, forcing end-client information into names, free text, or nowhere.

recurrence: Independent August 2026 requests expose a recurring two-party mismatch: time is tracked one way while billing needs payer and end-client context.
current_workaround: Encode the end customer in task names, use custom spreadsheet columns, or assemble time proof manually before invoicing.
incumbents_and_gap: Toggl, Harvest, Kimai, and Invoice Ninja track time or invoices, but do not make payer-to-end-client work attribution and a compact proof pack the primary object.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PWA with payer, end client, work order, timer/manual entries, deliverable links, and a one-click client-neutral PDF/CSV worklog. Non-goals: employee monitoring, screenshots, payroll, invoicing, or a full PSA.
success_measure: At least 75% of pilot time entries carry both payer and end-client attribution, and monthly invoice support packs take under five minutes to produce.
monetization: one-time — a contractor-owned record should continue to work even after a client engagement ends.
constraints: Do not capture activity telemetry; keep data local/exportable; ensure shared PDFs can omit end-client information where confidentiality requires it.
why_distinct: The core is dual-party attribution plus billable proof, not a generic timer.

title: Client Request Catalog
user: A tiny service or goods business that wants existing clients to request a priced service, POA item, or repeat order without a full ecommerce shop.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Ask HN validation request names invoicing, purchases, inventory, expenses, quotes, and cash sales as the everyday administrative mix for a small business.
A user asks for a client portal where an existing client can select visible products to request a quote or generate/pay an invoice, including POA and stock cases.

recurrence: A 2025 small-business workflow report and a 2026 self-service request independently point to a gap between internal inventory/quotes and a client-friendly request surface.
current_workaround: Take repeat requests by WhatsApp/email, circulate a PDF price list, or build a full online store that does not fit quote-first work.
incumbents_and_gap: Shopify and WooCommerce assume checkout; Invoice Ninja has a requested portal enhancement. Neither is a small, quote-first catalog for a known client list with mixed fixed/POA offerings.
smallest_useful_product: A branded single-page catalog with client-specific visibility, fixed-price or Request a Quote buttons, stock note, and a request inbox exportable to CSV/PDF. Non-goals: payment processing, public marketplace discovery, warehouse management, and full ecommerce.
success_measure: In a 60-day pilot, repeat-client requests submitted without back-and-forth exceed 40% and each request reaches a quote-ready state in under two minutes.
monetization: subscription — hosted client-facing links, access controls, and notifications have an ongoing operating cost.
constraints: Prevent public exposure of private pricing; use expiring client links and GDPR-style deletion/export; do not claim live stock unless manually confirmed.
why_distinct: It sits before the quote, serving repeat clients without turning a service business into an ecommerce implementation project.

title: Tax Evidence Pack
user: A sole trader who needs to turn expenses, receipts, invoice PDFs, and reimbursement proof into a reviewable tax-year package.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A small-business bookkeeping launch targets the manual work of collecting invoices/receipts from email and matching them to bank transactions.
An Actual Budget feature request says notes are insufficient for tax/audit evidence and explicitly asks for receipt/invoice attachments and an exportable tax-support package.

recurrence: Two independent 2026 bookkeeping reports identify document evidence—not merely transaction categorization—as the unresolved tax-prep step.
current_workaround: Attach files in a bookkeeping SaaS, put filenames in transaction notes, retain a folder tree, or hunt through email at tax time.
incumbents_and_gap: QuickBooks, Xero, Wave, FreshBooks, and Zoho Books attach documents, but exports are tied to a subscription/accounting workflow. A lightweight local binder can work alongside any ledger.
smallest_useful_product: Encrypted local desktop app: drag receipts/invoices, tag tax year/category/transaction reference, flag missing evidence, and export a read-only PDF index plus original-file ZIP. Non-goals: OCR, tax calculation, bank sync, or filing returns.
success_measure: At year-end, pilot users can produce a complete accountant-requested evidence pack in under 15 minutes with fewer than 5% of tagged expenses missing support.
monetization: one-time — users should retain access to their audit evidence without a recurring accounting subscription.
constraints: Encrypt files at rest; no cloud upload by default; preserve originals and hashes; clearly state that organization is not tax advice or compliant record retention in every jurisdiction.
why_distinct: It produces a portable evidence package from any bookkeeping system rather than replacing bookkeeping.

title: Owner Cash Check
user: An owner-operated new business that needs a weekly answer to what cash is committed, expected, and safe to spend without adopting enterprise forecasting.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ask HN asks what people use for business budgeting after a personal budgeting app became inadequate once the business needed transaction-level payment-platform insight.
A feature request for a persistent transaction inspector says fast inline editing loses the detail/context needed for sequential financial review.

recurrence: Two August 2026 sources show the handoff from personal finance tooling to business decisions is both common and poorly served by transaction lists alone.
current_workaround: Use a personal budget app, spreadsheet, or accounting dashboard and manually infer the next few weeks of commitments.
incumbents_and_gap: YNAB/Actual organize transactions; QuickBooks/Xero report accounting history; Float and Pulse are more elaborate forecasts. The gap is an owner’s compact, local weekly decision screen.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PWA where the owner enters account balance, dated committed outgoings, expected invoice dates, and a reserve; it displays 13-week low point, confidence labels, and a weekly check-in. Non-goals: bank aggregation, accounting ledger, forecasting AI, or investment advice.
success_measure: In 8 weeks, 80% of pilot users complete a weekly check-in and accurately flag every week where projected cash falls below their chosen reserve.
monetization: one-time — manual local forecasting should be useful without linking financial accounts or subscribing.
constraints: No bank credentials; local encryption/export; label estimates clearly and avoid claims of financial advice.
why_distinct: It is a decision-oriented near-term cash view, not a budgeting replacement or a thin AI forecast.

title: Guest Booking Confirm
user: A microbusiness taking appointments from people who should not need to create an account, and who need a clear confirmation/reminder trail.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ask HN asks how small businesses really handle appointment reminders; the reply identifies state synchronization rather than mere sending as the gap, often patched with calendar plus SMS automation.
An Odoo appointment user reports that a public visitor hits an unexplained login requirement when booking and asks for either anonymous booking or a clear registration path.

recurrence: A 2025 public-booking failure and a 2026 reminder-state discussion point to the same trust-critical boundary: guest intent, confirmed appointment, and reminder status.
current_workaround: Ask clients to register, take bookings by phone/WhatsApp, or connect a calendar and SMS service through Zapier.
incumbents_and_gap: Calendly, Square Appointments, Fresha, and Odoo are broad schedulers; their account, payment, and integration assumptions overwhelm a single service provider that only needs reliable guest confirmation state.
smallest_useful_product: A mobile-first booking page with no account, owner-approved time requests, single-use confirm/reschedule/cancel links, ICS attachment, and a local reminder checklist. Non-goals: payments, staff rota optimization, marketing CRM, or automated SMS sending.
success_measure: At least 95% of accepted guest requests have an explicit confirmation status, and no-show follow-ups attributable to an unclear booking state fall by 30% in 60 days.
monetization: freemium — a limited free calendar validates the workflow; hosted links and multi-staff calendars justify a paid tier.
constraints: Collect only contact data necessary for booking; give a clear consent notice and deletion window; handle timezone/DST correctly; do not market it as medical-grade scheduling.
why_distinct: It treats guest confirmation state as the product, rather than adding another full scheduling platform.

title: Scan Count Pad
user: A single-location shop or maker that needs to count/adjust stock at the shelf with a phone or Bluetooth scanner, even when connectivity is poor.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A lightweight inventory launch says small businesses are stuck between messy Google Sheets with no mobile scanning and expensive, overcomplicated enterprise software.
A Grocy user asks to scan with a Bluetooth handheld scanner on a mounted tablet and land directly on an item for fast add/consume actions.

recurrence: Two 2026 sources independently describe the same physical workflow: staff standing by stock with a scanner but no lightweight mobile count interface.
current_workaround: Use a paper tally then spreadsheet, type product names into a web inventory app, or buy a POS/ERP scanner module.
incumbents_and_gap: Google Sheets is flexible but poor at scanning; Grocy and Inventory/POS suites are broader systems. A count session optimized for scanner input and later import is missing.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PWA: import SKU/barcode CSV, choose a count session, scan/tap quantity, flag unknowns and variance, then export adjustments as CSV. Non-goals: POS, supplier ordering, live multi-site inventory, or camera-based AI recognition.
success_measure: A pilot completes a 100-SKU count at least 40% faster than spreadsheet entry and resolves 95% of unknown scans before export.
monetization: one-time — a local count utility should work at a back-room bench without ongoing per-seat fees.
constraints: Camera permission only while scanning; local-first storage and CSV import/export; never treat a scanned code as authoritative without user reconciliation.
why_distinct: It is a deliberately narrow physical stock-count tool, not an inventory database or POS clone.

title: Stock Photo Aliases
user: A small stock keeper whose helpers must recognize one internal product despite different brands, packages, or barcodes arriving on the shelf.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A builder created local inventory/production management for a parent’s small manufacturer specifically to track stock and reorder levels without subscription or data-sovereignty concerns.
A feature request describes one product arriving in different brands/barcodes/packages and asks for multiple images so helpers can visually identify it during stock management.

recurrence: The 2025 feature request supplies a concrete helper-facing failure mode; a 2026 small-manufacturer project confirms stock tools are still built to escape spreadsheet/subscription tradeoffs.
current_workaround: Create duplicate SKUs, tape a photo to shelving, add brand names to notes, or explain substitutions verbally to helpers.
incumbents_and_gap: Grocy requests multiple images, while ERPs model variants extensively. For a tiny business, there is no simple visual alias card that maps many supplied packages to one countable item.
smallest_useful_product: Local PWA: create a canonical stock item, attach multiple package photos/barcodes/nicknames, print a shelf card/QR code, and export the alias map. Non-goals: image recognition, supplier catalog sync, ecommerce listings, or full inventory accounting.
success_measure: After two weeks, helpers correctly map at least 95% of sampled package variants to the canonical item without asking the owner.
monetization: one-time — visual reference is a durable local asset and should not need a hosted inventory subscription.
constraints: Photos may show labels/vendor data; store locally by default; confirm barcode ownership/use rights; provide printable accessibility labels rather than image-only cues.
why_distinct: It solves product recognition across package substitutions, not stock valuation or SKU management broadly.

title: Stocktake Reconcile
user: A tiny ecommerce, workshop, or stockroom operator who needs to turn a physical count into explainable variance adjustments with correct units.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An inventory-app builder asks warehouse/ecommerce operators for feedback on receiving, bin locations, pick/pack/ship, and upcoming QuickBooks integration.
An InvenTree stocktake user reports a quantity validation error for a kilogram item even when entering 2.85, showing how unit-level friction can block reconciliation.

recurrence: A 2026 inventory workflow launch and a separate 2026 stocktake defect both put reconciliation at the junction of physical operations and accounting accuracy.
current_workaround: Overwrite quantity in the inventory system, make a manual spreadsheet adjustment, or postpone the count while investigating unit errors.
incumbents_and_gap: InvenTree, Odoo, and ecommerce inventory tools store stock, but their stocktake modules are embedded in larger systems and can make a simple audited variance review brittle.
smallest_useful_product: CSV-in/CSV-out desktop utility that compares expected and counted stock, supports integer/weight/decimal units, requires a reason for material variance, and emits an adjustment journal plus signed count report. Non-goals: warehouse execution, ecommerce sync, accounting posting, or multi-user live stock.
success_measure: A pilot completes a 200-line stocktake with every adjustment carrying a unit and reason, and can reproduce the final adjustment CSV from the saved count report.
monetization: one-time — a periodic reconciliation tool has no inherent ongoing service requirement.
constraints: Validate decimal precision without silently rounding; retain original import plus immutable export hash; never calculate tax/accounting entries; keep files local.
why_distinct: It is a portable reconciliation and audit layer that complements, rather than replaces, an inventory system.
